etymology: From the Old French ester, to stand - the order that makes a thing stand still while it is argued about.
effect: Stops the thing from happening while it is being argued about, and puts the status quo back where it was.
costs: A motion, a bond, and a judge willing to be the one who halted it.
failure: The stay that expires quietly, and the harm ruled not irreparable because it has already happened.
tell: An order with a date on it
A bond that makes delay expensive
A status quo that actually holds

confused_with.tell: The night docket moves while nobody is watching; the stay is the thing that makes it wait until somebody is.

senses: The order that suspends an action while a challenge is heard: a rule, an execution, a demolition, a transfer. It is the procedural equivalent of a hand on the arm, granted or refused by a judge who has to say why.

It works because it changes who bears the risk of the delay. Without a stay the challenger loses by default - the thing is done before the argument is heard - so the remedy is not the ruling, it is the preservation of the possibility of one.
example: *"The **stay** came through at four in the afternoon, the demolition crew stood down, and the hearing that followed was about the building instead of about the rubble."*
